focus_territories: Graph theory and mathematical structures (Lattice, Vertex) — technically precise, maps directly to DAG architecture
Convergence and flow dynamics (Vortex, Orbit, Helix) — captures the iterative, converging nature of task execution
Geometric and structural metaphors (Axis, Vertex) — sharp, modern, CLI-friendly
Biological and natural systems (Helix, Pulse) — implies organic growth and rhythmic execution
winning_phonetic_shapes: Two syllables, hard consonants: Vertex, Lattice, Vortex, Orbit, Helix
Single syllable with strong ending: Flux, Pulse (though both have collision issues)
X-ending names feel sharp and modern: Vertex, Vortex, Helix, Flux, Apex (all survivors or strong rejections)
morphemes_to_explore: -ex/-ix endings (vertex, helix, apex) — sharp, technical, modern
Graph/network terms: node, edge, path, graph, mesh, web, net
Convergence terms: focal, nexus, locus, crux
Iteration/spiral terms: cycle, loop, coil, spiral, whorl
Verification/proof terms: proof, verify, attest, certify, seal
morphemes_to_avoid: Generic orchestration terms: flow, pipe, stream, task, work, run, exec
Overused AI terms: neural, cognitive, synapse, cortex, brain
Enterprise bloat: catalyst, substrate, platform, solution, system
creative_prompts: Explore mathematical/CS terms that are precise but not obscure: what are the sharp, ownable terms from graph theory, type theory, or formal verification?
Find natural phenomena that embody 'verified convergence': what natural systems iterate toward stable, verifiable states?
Look for short, punchy words (1-2 syllables) with hard consonants that feel like CLI commands you'd want to type
Explore Latin/Greek roots for convergence, verification, and iteration — but keep them pronounceable and memorable
Consider portmanteaus or blends that combine 'verify' + 'converge' concepts without feeling forced
Research lesser-known geometric or topological terms that map to DAG concepts: what are the ownable technical terms?
